chunks: And Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ḥarīz, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The abandoned child is free. If he wishes, he may assign his allegiance to those who raised him, and if he wishes, to others.

key_terms.رَبَّوْهُ: those who raised and brought him up
key_terms.وَلَاءَهُ: his bond of allegiance or clientage

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a foundling in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a foundling is legally free and not bound by servile status. It also affirms that his bond of wala' may be assigned by his own choice, whether to those who raised him or to others.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3531 - It is narrated from Hammad bin Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdullah (as):
"The abandoned child (foundling) is free. If he wishes, he may assign his allegiance to those who raised him, or if he wishes, to others."
